newsitem.title: CHILE: Union members at Escondida mine vote on pay offer.
newsitem.headline: Union members at Escondida mine vote on pay offer.

text.p: Union members at Chile's giant Escondida copper pit were voting Tuesday in a secret ballot whether to accept the company's final pay offer or go on strike, said union officials.
Officials said voting started at 1400 local/1900 GMT at the mine site and in Antofagasta. The result should be known at around 2200 local.
The strike vote involves only the 350 of the mine's 2,000 strong workforce who are members of the pit union.
Union leaders have recommended members reject the company's offer to increase wages in line with inflation.
The union had demanded a seven percent increase in real terms.
Escondida, considered the world's largest copper mine, is owned by Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd and RTZ Corp plc. It produced over 800,000 tonnes of copper in 1996.
